COMMON INTEREST DEVELOPMENT FORMATION — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Acme Development, LLC · Sunset Terrace Condominiums

COMMON INTEREST DEVELOPMENT FORMATION — INTRODUCTION AND SCOPE
This information sheet describes, in general terms, how a common interest development is created under California's Davis-Stirling Common Interest Development Act, Civil Code § 4000 et seq. It concerns a proposed or existing common interest development to be known as Sunset Terrace Condominiums, located at or encompassing 789 Terrace Way, San Diego, CA 92101 in San Diego County County, California, to be created (or previously created) by Acme Development, LLC as declarant. This document addresses formation — the statutory definition of a common interest development, the recorded declaration that creates it, the recording steps that bring it into existence, the requirement that an association be formed to manage it, and the association's statutory authority to levy assessments once formed. It is distinct from, and does not address, a seller's document-disclosure obligations to a buyer of an existing separate interest (Civil Code § 4525 et seq.) or an association's lien and foreclosure remedies for delinquent assessments (Civil Code §§ 5650–5740), both addressed in other documents in this library. This sheet is informational only. It does not itself create a common interest development, does not record any document, does not form or incorporate any association, and does not determine whether any specific declaration, condominium plan, map, articles, bylaws, or assessment described in connection with Sunset Terrace Condominiums complies with the statutory requirements it describes.

THE STATUTORY DEFINITION OF A COMMON INTEREST DEVELOPMENT
California law defines "common interest development" as a specific, closed list of four project types — not a general catch-all for any residential development with shared ownership or a homeowners association. Civil Code § 4100 provides: "'Common interest development' means any of the following: (a) A community apartment project. (b) A condominium project. (c) A planned development. (d) A stock cooperative." Each of these four terms is itself separately defined elsewhere in the Act. Whether the project contemplated in connection with Sunset Terrace Condominiums falls within one of these four statutory categories, and which one, is a factual and legal question this document does not resolve.

  "(a) A community apartment project. (b) A condominium project. (c) A planned development. (d) A stock cooperative."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 4100(a)-(d) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 4100(a)-(d) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=4100.)
  Known gap: Both quoted sentences come from the same statutory section, Civil Code § 4100; they are not independent sections corroborating each other, though the closing sentence enumerating subdivisions (a) through (d) is itself the complete operative definition, not an excerpt combined from elsewhere. This document does not separately quote the individual definitions of "community apartment project," "condominium project," "planned development," or "stock cooperative" (found at Civil Code §§ 4105, 4125, 4175, and 4190, respectively) beyond what this clause's companion clauses touch on for condominium projects; a reader needing the precise statutory definition of one of the other three categories should consult that section directly. This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of California's Davis-Stirling Common Interest Development Act's threshold definition — not a claim about which state's law governs a specific project; other states define comparable development types differently or not at all.

THE DECLARATION — DEFINITION AND REQUIRED STATUTORY CONTENT
The declaration is the foundational recorded document that establishes a common interest development's covenants, conditions, and restrictions. Civil Code § 4135 defines it: "'Declaration' means the document, however denominated, that contains the information required by Sections 4250 and 4255." Civil Code § 4250(a) states what a declaration recorded on or after January 1, 1986 must contain: "A declaration, recorded on or after January 1, 1986, shall contain a legal description of the common interest development, and a statement that the common interest development is a community apartment project, condominium project, planned development, stock cooperative, or combination thereof. The declaration shall additionally set forth the name of the association and the restrictions on the use or enjoyment of any portion of the common interest development that are intended to be enforceable equitable servitudes." Beyond that required minimum, § 4250(b) permits the declaration to address other matters: "The declaration may contain any other matters the declarant or the members consider appropriate." If a declaration for Sunset Terrace Condominiums has been recorded, its recording information is stated as: Recorded October 1, 2026, Instrument No. 2026-0123456.

  "A declaration, recorded on or after January 1, 1986, shall contain a legal description of the common interest development, and a statement that the common interest development is a community apartment project, condominium project, planned development, stock cooperative, or combination thereof. The declaration shall additionally set forth the name of the association and the restrictions on the use or enjoyment of any portion of the common interest development that are intended to be enforceable equitable servitudes."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 4250(a)-(b) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 4250(a)-(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=4250.)

The citations to § 4135 and § 4250(a)-(b) are to two separate statutory sections; § 4250(a) and (b) are subsections of the same section, quoted together because (b) clarifies that (a)'s list is a floor, not a ceiling, on permissible content. This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of California's Davis-Stirling Common Interest Development Act's declaration requirements — not a claim about which state's law governs a specific project, and not a determination that any specific declaration recorded or proposed for the development named in this document in fact contains the statutorily required content.

FORMATION MECHANICS — WHAT MUST BE RECORDED TO CREATE THE CID
A common interest development is not created merely by a declarant's intent, a marketing plan, or an unrecorded set of restrictions; the Act ties formation to specific recorded documents. Civil Code § 4200 provides: "This act applies and a common interest development is created whenever a separate interest coupled with an interest in the common area or membership in the association is, or has been, conveyed, provided all of the following are recorded: (a) A declaration. (b) A condominium plan, if any exists. (c) A final map or parcel map, if Division 2 (commencing with Section 66410) of Title 7 of the Government Code requires the recording of either a final map or parcel map for the common interest development." Where the project is a condominium project, the recorded condominium plan referenced in § 4200(b) has its own required content: Civil Code § 4285 provides that "[a] condominium plan shall contain all of the following: (a) A description or survey map of a condominium project, which shall refer to or show monumentation on the ground." If a condominium plan and/or final or parcel map affecting Sunset Terrace Condominiums has been recorded, its recording information is stated as: Condominium Plan recorded October 1, 2026, Instrument No. 2026-0123457.

(c) A final map or parcel map, if Division 2 (commencing with Section 66410) of Title 7 of the Government Code requires the recording of either a final map or parcel map for the common interest development."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 4200 (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 4200 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=4200.)
  "A condominium plan shall contain all of the following: (a) A description or survey map of a condominium project, which shall refer to or show monumentation on the ground."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 4285(a) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 4285(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=4285.)

The citations to § 4200 and § 4285 are to two separate statutory sections. This clause does not address whether a final map or parcel map is required for the development named in this document under the Subdivision Map Act (Government Code § 66410 et seq.), which § 4200(c) itself cross-references and which this document does not independently research. THE ASSOCIATION'S MANDATORY FORMATION AND WHAT GOVERNS IT
California law does not leave it optional whether a common interest development has a managing association — it requires one. Civil Code § 4800 provides: "A common interest development shall be managed by an association that may be incorporated or unincorporated. The association may be referred to as an owners' association or a community association." The association's own governance is not left to informal practice; it is defined by a specific set of "governing documents." Civil Code § 4150 provides: "'Governing documents' means the declaration and any other documents, such as bylaws, operating rules, articles of incorporation, or articles of association, which govern the operation of the common interest development or association." If Sunset Terrace Condominiums's association is to be, or has been, formed as Sunset Terrace Owners Association, and if it is or is intended to be incorporated, that status is stated as: incorporated as a nonprofit mutual benefit corporation.

ASSESSMENTS — THE FORMATION-STAGE STATUTORY BASIS FOR THE POWER TO LEVY
Once a common interest development and its association exist, California law imposes an affirmative statutory duty on the association to levy assessments, and separately caps what it may charge. Civil Code § 5600(a) provides: "Except as provided in Section 5605, the association shall levy regular and special assessments sufficient to perform its obligations under the governing documents and this act." Section 5600(b) adds a limiting principle: "An association shall not impose or collect an assessment or fee that exceeds the amount necessary to defray the costs for which it is levied." This clause addresses only the association's underlying statutory authority and duty to levy assessments once the common interest development and association are formed; it does not address how an unpaid assessment becomes a recorded, enforceable lien against a specific owner's separate interest, the pre-lien notice an association must give, lien priority, or the foreclosure process — all addressed in this library's separate HOA Assessment Lien and Foreclosure information sheet, which governs collection and enforcement rather than formation-stage authority.

  "An association shall not impose or collect an assessment or fee that exceeds the amount necessary to defray the costs for which it is levied."
  — Cal. Civ. Code § 5600(b) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 5600(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=5600.)
  Known gap: Both quoted provisions are subsections of the same statutory section, Civil Code § 5600(a) and (b); they are not independent sections corroborating each other, and are disclosed together here because they state, respectively, the duty to levy and the limit on how much may be levied. This is one state's statute, used as real evidence of California's Davis-Stirling Common Interest Development Act's assessment-levy authority — not a claim about which state's law governs a specific project, and not a determination of whether any specific assessment levied or proposed by the association named in this document in fact complies with these or other statutory requirements.

DECLARANT'S FORMATION STATEMENT
This Formation Statement is prepared by Acme Development, LLC, as declarant, in connection with the proposed or existing common interest development known as Sunset Terrace Condominiums, located at or encompassing 789 Terrace Way, San Diego, CA 92101 in San Diego County County, California. The development is stated to be a: condominium project. The association to be formed or already formed to manage the development is stated to be: Sunset Terrace Owners Association. This statement records, for reference, background information about the intended or completed formation of Sunset Terrace Condominiums as a common interest development under California's Davis-Stirling Common Interest Development Act. It is not itself a declaration, a condominium plan, a final map or parcel map, articles of incorporation, or bylaws; it does not record or create any of those documents; and it does not, by itself, create a common interest development, form or incorporate any association, or establish any assessment obligation. Whether Sunset Terrace Condominiums has been, or will be, validly created as a common interest development depends on the actual recording of a declaration and any other documents the Act requires, and on the actual formation of an association to manage it — steps this statement does not perform.
